explanation: Beckoning with a single crooked index finger can come across as curt or overly commanding in Brazil, particularly toward strangers or in professional settings — Brazilians more commonly wave someone over with the whole hand. That said, it is not treated as the severe insult it is in places like the Philippines; even calling a waiter over with a raised hand is completely normal and expected in Brazilian restaurants.
local_tip: To call someone over politely, wave with your whole hand rather than crooking a single finger, especially with someone you don't know well.

also_check.note: Beckoning with the index finger is seen as rude, closer to calling an animal; a palm-down hand wave is used instead.
Beckoning with a finger is considered highly offensive and can be seen as a challenge; a gentle palm-down wave is used instead.
Common in casual settings, but can seem dismissive or condescending in formal or professional contexts.
